findings.severity_note: Lowered from high: no substantial advertising or session-replay evidence cited (a tracking cookie, activity after reject, or 3+ requests to an actual tracking domain; a tag loader like Google Tag Manager alone doesn't count), so an exemption or innocent explanation is plausible.
findings.title: Advertising-related request occurred before consent
findings.detail: Two requests identified as Google advertising activity were sent to googletagmanager.com before any consent choice was made. The audit found no banner or successful rejection action, so the requests were not preceded by valid consent.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6; UK GDPR Articles 5(1)(a), 6 and 7
findings.policy_quote: When you first visit the Website and we notify you about our use of Cookies, you can choose not to consent to such use.
findings.reasoning: Advertising-related tracking before consent is a clear PECR concern and is not covered by the limited analytics or functionality exceptions. This is high severity because the evidence identifies the activity as advertising and the policy says visitors can choose not to consent before cookies are used.
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EU GDPR Articles 5(1)(a), 6 and 7

findings.title: Accept is one click, but we found no way to reject
findings.detail: The banner offers "Cookie Policy", but our automated check could not find any reject or decline option. (This may be a limit of our check, so treat it as something to verify.)
findings.law: ICO cookie guidance (refusing must be as easy as accepting)
findings.law_eu: EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on consent; EDPB Cookie Banner Taskforce report (2023)

ai_review.summary: The audit found clear evidence of Google advertising-related requests before any consent choice, creating a high-severity PECR concern. The cookie policy states that visitors can choose not to consent, but the audit found no banner or successful rejection mechanism and still observed advertising activity. The supplied policies also provide only limited information about rights, retention and complaints.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: False. Reject clicked successfully: False. Method: failed. Buttons clicked: none.
E2: Tracker Google (Advertising): 2 requests before consent, 0 after reject, to googletagmanager.com.
E3: Privacy policy: https://privacy.informa.com/about/en/. Companies it names: Transcend. Contact email found: None.

E5: Automated check (low): Accept is one click, but we found no way to reject. The banner offers "Cookie Policy", but our automated check could not find any reject or decline option. (This may be a limit of our check, so treat it as something to verify.)
